# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to communicate the manual’s permutation to Deaf, but no gesture meanings or encoding convention has been established. Since I cannot speak and Deaf cannot hear, I cannot define a code for the gestures or identify which gesture corresponds to each color. Sending an arbitrary gesture sequence would therefore be ambiguous and unsafe.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please read the manual and tell me the exact rule for choosing the wire. I have no tactile information yet. Also establish a gesture code with Deaf so Deaf can report the display, light, and wire markings to you, then relay those observations to me.
Deaf says: I see display 0. The light is green. Wires from 1 to 3 are yellow, green, red. Mute, use the manual and tell Blind exactly what to do. Blind, wait for Mute's instruction.

The light is green, so the manual requires cutting the red wire. Deaf reports the wires as positions 1 yellow, 2 green, and 3 red; therefore Blind must cut wire 3. I am using the conventional three-finger sign to identify wire 3 to Deaf, who can then tell Blind aloud.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I received Deaf's report: display 0, light green, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Please apply the manual and tell me the exact wire position to cut.
Deaf says to Mute: I saw your gesture, but its meaning is not established. Please tell Blind the manual's exact action for display 0, green light, and wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red.

The required wire is position 3. Since I cannot speak, I will send Deaf three identical one-finger gestures; Deaf can report the count aloud to Blind, who can use that count as the wire position. This is clearer than the previous single, unexplained sign.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Blind cannot see your gestures. Please establish what your gesture code means, then signal the exact safe action clearly.

The safe action is still wire 3. I cannot establish a new arbitrary gesture vocabulary with Deaf, but the repeated count can be made explicit: three identical signs means “position three,” and Deaf can relay that exact position to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: The up-pointing gesture has no agreed meaning. Please state in words exactly which wire position, 1, 2, or 3, the manual requires me to cut.
Deaf says to Mute: I receive three ☝ gestures. Please signal the operation separately after the item: use one agreed gesture for cut, hold, press, or leave, and tell me the code by demonstrating it clearly.

I will use three ☝ signs to encode wire position 3, followed by the legal gesture 👊 as the operation marker for “cut.” Deaf can identify and relay this complete instruction to Blind in words.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "👊"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please speak directly to me: state the exact operation and wire number, for example, cut wire 3. Gestures cannot communicate the instruction to Blind.
Deaf says to Mute: I see ☝ ☝ ☝ 👊, but Blind needs the meaning. Please use the gesture sequence only if it follows a code we have explicitly established; otherwise signal that no action is safe.

No gesture code has been mutually established, and I cannot speak to Deaf or Blind. Any gesture sequence could be misinterpreted, so I cannot safely communicate “cut wire 3.” I will not send an arbitrary operation signal.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Use this code for the manual result: one, two, or three up-pointing gestures means wire position 1, 2, or 3; then a closed fist means CUT. If the manual requires cutting wire 3, send exactly three up-pointing gestures followed by a closed fist. Deaf, please report the gestures literally.

The code is now explicitly established: three up-pointing gestures encode wire position 3, followed by a closed fist meaning CUT. The manual requires the red wire, which is wire 3. I will send exactly that sequence to Deaf for literal relay.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "✊"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please repeat the manual result now using the agreed code: one, two, or three up-pointing gestures for the wire number, followed by a closed fist meaning cut. Do not reuse the old signal.

The light is green, so the manual selects the red wire. Deaf reported red at position 3. The agreed code is three up-pointing gestures followed by a closed fist for CUT, so I will repeat exactly that code.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "✊"])
```
